reasoning.Student A:
My goal is to maximize my value, given the school priorities. I know that I will be matched to my favorite school within my "obtainable set."

School y offers the highest value ($75) and I have the highest priority (1) there. Therefore, y is very likely to be in my obtainable set.

School w has a value of $66 and I have the highest priority (1) there. Therefore, w is also very likely to be in my obtainable set.

School x has a value of $64 and I have the second highest priority (2) there. It is less likely to be in my obtainable set than y and w.

School z has the lowest value ($44) and I have the second highest priority (2) there. It is the least desirable option.

Given these considerations, I will rank the schools in decreasing order of value, starting with y, then w, then x, then z. This ensures that if y is in my obtainable set, I will be matched to y. If y is not in my obtainable set, but w is, then I will be matched to w, and so on. This strategy maximizes my expected value.
